title: Instrumentation sentinel: lightweight cross-channel request attestation and trace hook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: browser and edge SDKs currently lose request context when requests cross channel boundaries (fetch -> Worker -> WebSocket/SSE/WebTransport) which breaks end-to-end traces and inflates orphan spans. Goal: implement a lightweight instrumentation sentinel (SDK + middleware + tiny runtime hook) that consistently attaches a stable request attestation token and propagates a sampling decision across channels with minimal payload overhead and no site-breaking headers. The sentinel must: 1) support fetch, XHR, Service Worker, dedicated/Shared Workers, WebSocket, SSE, and WebTransport; 2) fall back to cookie/localStorage when header injection is impossible (e.g., cross-origin iframes without COOP/COEP); 3) include a compact provenance stamp (crc32 + truncated origin fingerprint + epoch) that is safe to include in logs and diagnostic traces; 4) elect a coordinator for multi-request fanout (e.g., longpoll + xhr) to avoid duplicate root spans; 5) provide developer-facing opt-in shim for legacy apps and opt-out control for privacy-sensitive flows. Non-goals: full OTLP implementation inside the browser, heavy cryptographic signatures, or storing full trace payloads client-side.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a single function instrument() that attaches attestation token to outbound requests where possible
A deterministic coordinator election prevents duplicate root spans for fanout requests in at least 95% of synthetic tests
Token size < 48 bytes when encoded in header; < 96 bytes when stored in cookie/localStorage fallback
End-to-end traces remain linked for cross-channel flows in the integrated suite (browser + worker + edge-proxy) in > 98% of runs
No new CSP violations in apps with default Content-Security-Policy (report-only mode tested)
design_decisions: Use a compact attestation token: base64url(trunc(HMAC(origin+timestamp), 8) + ':' + epoch32 + ':' + sampler-bit) to avoid expensive crypto and long headers
Prefer header injection 'x-rdwd-attest' when same-origin or CORS allows 'Access-Control-Expose-Headers', fall back to 'rdwd_attest' cookie with Secure+SameSite=Lax where headers cannot be set
Coordinator election implemented as first-writer-wins using session-scoped ephemeral id in worker scope; deterministic tie-breaker is lexicographic on origin+timestamp

Sampling decision made once at the root request; propagated via attestation token sampler-bit. SDK offers a pluggable sampler hook for advanced sampling policies (probabilistic, deterministic by user-id hash)
Avoid adding large polyfills; implement most behavior with tiny runtime checks and leverage Service Worker interception where available
test_plan: Unit tests for token encoding/decoding and sampler-bit semantics (CI)
Integration harness: playwright scenarios across fetch, worker postMessage, service worker fetch handler, WebSocket handshake and mid-flight messages
Synthetic fuzz: 10k permutations of worker handoffs with network delay/jitter to validate coordinator election stability
E2E lab: deploy to staging with the edge-proxy and run the trace-reconstruction job against sampling=0.1 and sampling=1.0
Privacy QA: ensure attestation token does not contain PII and verify cookie fallback honors SameSite and Secure flags
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'instrumentation_sentinel' runtime flag (console toggle + env var for private deployments)
Canary: 1% of hosted customers by handshake region; observe new trace linkage metric and client-side error rate for 48h
If stable, expand 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with metric checks at each step
Dedicated customers will receive a migration doc and opt-in sample config for VPC/private deployments
Post-rollout: bake for 30 days then flip GA flag and enable automatic integration with Console dashboards
dashboard_items_to_create: Latency vs linked-trace rate: identify regressions when linked traces drop and tail latency rises
Attestation fallback heatmap by origin and client version
Coordinator conflict rate timeseries with debug drilldowns
Sampled request waterfall view for cross-channel flows (fetch -> worker -> websocket)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cross-origin policies block header injection -> Mitigation: cookie fallback with clear opt-out and documented CSP guidance
Risk: Performance impact on cold path -> Mitigation: lazy initialization and no-op fastpath when instrumentation disabled
Risk: Token fingerprinting could be abused -> Mitigation: truncate fingerprints, rotate epoch every 24h, and document privacy properties
Risk: Duplicate root spans if coordinator election fails under extreme concurrency -> Mitigation: add a server-side dedupe window and probabilistic backoff in coordinator

2025-03-08 Sasha Patel (sec): Reviewed threat model. Requested explicit privacy doc and ensured token contains no user identifiers. Also requested toggles for telemetry emission frequency.
2025-03-09 Design review: UX for devs — instrument() exposes a telemetry opt-in banner and clear API for overriding sampler. Design suggests concise developer console message on failure modes.

2025-03-11 Diego Martinez: Addressed PR feedback: reduced token length, improved cookie fallback atomicity, added unit tests for cross-origin header exposure cases. New PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1451

2025-03-12 QA: Integration tests failing intermittently for WebTransport handshake scenario under network jitter. Investigating coordinator edge case where postMessage arrives out-of-order. Added jitter buffer in worker handshake code as temporary mitigation.
